surfaces.part: tree canopy (foliage mass, rounded blob with highlights top-left and shadow at the bottom)

answer.evidence: Organic broadleaf tree. The canopy is a rounded volumetric mass (rows 4-48) with light highlight clusters on the upper left and top, mid-tone body, and dark shadow underneath (rows 43-50, L~28). The width profile widens from 3 at row 4 to 44 at row 26, then narrows to 19 at row 48. This gives the 3/4 dome look of a canopy seen from above and the front. The trunk (rows 49-63) flares at the base with root buttresses and has a visible front face. It is drawn with a lit left side and a darker right side. As an organic object it has no flat structural top; the foliage mass carries its volume through shading rather than a hard edge line, so it reads as a three-quarter view and not as a flat elevation or a top-down slab.
